messages:
Mike - Support: Customer reported p99 jump for deepshift-v1 after today's tokenizer tweak. p95 ~600ms -> p99 ~3.2s for inputs >12k tokens. Some requests 504'd.

Mike - Support: Happened around 13:04 UTC. Customer provided curl + payload. Attaching sample.

Julia (ML Eng): can you paste the sample request (headers + body) and the model variant they hit?

Mike - Support: sample below:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"deepshift-v1","input":"<~13k tokens...>","temperature":0.0}'
```

Anna (SRE): I'm seeing matching errors in our serving logs. High KV cache miss rate starting at 13:03:58 on deepshift-v1 shards in us-west1. Also repeated lines: `kernel: falling back to slow_attention_path for seq_len=12288` and `batcher: split into small batches due to token boundary`.

Anna (SRE): Example log snippet:
```
[13:04:02] shard=12 model=deepshift-v1 req_id=... kv_cache_hit=false seq_len=12560 kernel=slow_attention_path latency=3120ms
[13:04:03] shard=12 batcher=split tokens=12560 -> parts=3
```

Oliver (Platform): That `split into small batches` suggests the tokenizer change altered token alignment so many long inputs exceed our batchable prefix size -> causes multiple KV cache resets and slowpath kernel selection. Could be a change in byte-pair rules or added sentinel tokens.

Julia (ML Eng): Was this tokenizer tweak rolled to all variants or only the v1 release? We have `deepshift-v1-legacy` still using old tokenizer.

Mike - Support: Customer explicitly hit `deepshift-v1` (new tokenizer). They confirmed they tested against legacy earlier with no issue.

Oliver (Platform): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) route traffic from deepshift-v1 -> deepshift-v1-legacy for affected accounts; 2) enable KV-cache-warmup for long requests; 3) force model to use `fast_attention_path` heuristic by lowering seq threshold in config as a temporary knob. Any objections?

Anna (SRE): I'll start routing policy for the customer to legacy variant while we triage. Can also flip `kv_cache_warmup=true` in routing for their workspace.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered: routing change applied for workspace=acct-742. Old variant `deepshift-v1-legacy` now receives 100% for that workspace.

Mike - Support: Customer confirmed reduced errors immediately after rollback, but we still need root cause and a fix.

Julia (ML Eng): Repro steps for eng team: use the customer's payload with long context (>=12k tokens) against deepshift-v1 in staging, capture `kv_cache_hit` metrics and kernel path. repro-bot can run a quick harness.

repro-bot: Started batch run 50 requests long-context (12k-14k tokens) against staging deepshift-v1. Will post aggregated metrics in ~10m.

Anna (SRE): Observed in staging: KV cache miss rate jumps from 7% -> 68% after tokenizer change, p99 ~3.1s, many `slow_attention_path` entries. Also seeing more frequent `kvcache: invalidation due to token boundary mismatch`.

Julia (ML Eng): Sounds like tokenizer emits a different split causing kv cache key mismatches (prefix boundaries shifted). Two parallel fixes: a) revert tokenizer commit or b) add compatibility layer that normalizes token boundaries for KV cache (cheaper short-term: revert on deepshift-v1).

Oliver (Platform): We can also add a routing rule that pins long-context traffic to `*-legacy` until we ship a token-normalization patch. I'll prepare a config to scope by workspace and long_input flag.

Anna (SRE): Ops checklist I ran: increased worker pool to absorb backlog, disabled aggressive batching for that model to prevent huge multi-split work, applied routing to legacy. No service-wide impact observed.

Mike - Support: Customer grateful, but asks for ETA on permanent fix. Can we give timeline?

Julia (ML Eng): Plan: revert tokenizer on deepshift-v1 in next canary (2-4 hours), run regression tests for semantic parity, then reintroduce with token-normalization in 2-3 days. If we can implement normalization quicker, we'll try rollforward instead.

Oliver (Platform): I'll coordinate canary and also add a short-term config knob `max_seq_batchable=8192` to prevent splitting beyond our optimized kernel threshold. That reduces throughput but improves p99.

Anna (SRE): Post-routing metrics (13:18 UTC): p95 ~620ms, p99 ~880ms for the customer's traffic on legacy route. No 504s since routing change.

Mike - Support: Passing update to customer: they acknowledged and will keep testing. Marking incident as triaged; will keep open until tokenizer rollback or patch confirmed. :thumbsup:

Julia (ML Eng): Adding follow-up items: create an entry in onboarding checklist to run token-boundary smoke checks for any tokenizer changes; add unit tests that simulate long-context KV cache key stability.

Oliver (Platform): Filed infra task INF-4821 to add `token-boundary` metric and alert when kvcache invalidation crosses 10% for long inputs.

Anna (SRE): I'm oncall for next 2 hours. Ping @oncall if anything regresses.

Mike - Support: Thanks team. Will update thread when rollback/patch is complete.

(13:28) Mike - Support: closing interim triage — routing in place, customer notifications sent.
